title: Deterministic fail-closed PIT admissibility predicate
why_selected: The repository names this work itself. portfolio_automation/northstar/pit.py lines 13-14 state: 'This is the future anti-lookahead authority: Phase 0C will enforce evidence.known_at <= experiment.as_of.' That is the smallest useful atomic foundation task, it is required by the 0C exit gate (lookahead-audited PIT reads), and every other gateway capability (identity, provenance, revision safety) depends on having an admissibility decision to attach to.

justification: Pure contract-level predicate over the existing 0B PointInTime kernel. Adds no persistence, no vendor coupling, no production wiring, no authority. Directly serves the authoritative 0C exit gate.

acceptance_criteria: known_at == as_of is ADMITTED (boundary is inclusive, matching '<= as_of')
known_at one microsecond after as_of is REJECTED
known_at is None with basis 'unknown' is REJECTED with a distinct reason
a naive (tz-unaware) as_of is REJECTED with a distinct reason
known_at earlier than published_at is REJECTED as incoherent timing
decisions are reasons from a closed set, not free text
identical inputs always produce identical decisions
importing the module performs no I/O and reads no clock
escalation_conditions: canonical PIT semantics turn out to be ambiguous for a required rule -> ABSTAIN
a rule would require inventing semantics the 0B kernel does not define -> record NEXT_TASK_CANDIDATE and exclude it, do not guess
any requirement would need vendor, persistence or production scope -> STOP
taskspec.goal: Provide the EvidenceGateway's single deterministic decision: given a canonical PointInTime and an as-of instant, is this evidence admissible for a read as of that instant? Enforce the anti-lookahead authority named by portfolio_automation/northstar/pit.py: known_at <= as_of. Fail closed when timing is unknown or internally incoherent, and return an explicit machine-readable reason for every decision.
requirements: admissible iff known_at is present AND known_at <= as_of
known_at absent (basis 'unknown') is NOT admissible — fail closed, never treated as admissible-by-default
known_at strictly after as_of is NOT admissible (the core anti-lookahead rule)
as_of must be timezone-aware; a naive as_of is refused rather than coerced
every decision carries an explicit machine-readable reason code
the predicate is pure and deterministic: no clock read, no I/O, no network
0B canonical contracts are consumed, never modified
no vendor schema appears in the interface

title: Admit whole evidence at the gateway: identity + provenance binding
why_selected: Task 1 decides admissibility from a PIT envelope alone. A gateway that admits a PIT but never checks that the evidence it belongs to is self-consistent would let identity- or provenance-corrupted evidence through on correct timing. Foundation targets D (identity) and E (provenance) name exactly this, and it is the smallest increment that turns a predicate into an actual admission boundary.

justification: Pure validation over existing 0B contracts (EvidenceSnapshot, EvidenceRef, Provenance). No storage, no vendor, no production. Directly serves foundation targets D and E.

acceptance_criteria: a well-formed snapshot with known_at <= as_of is ADMITTED
a snapshot with future known_at is refused with the PIT reason, unchanged
a tampered payload (hash mismatch) is refused with an identity reason
a ref pointing at different content is refused with a ref-mismatch reason
identity/provenance checks run only after PIT, so timing refusals stay attributable to timing
malformed input returns a decision rather than raising
escalation_conditions: if enforcing identity requires modifying the 0B contract -> ABSTAIN
if a rule would need semantics 0B does not define -> record candidate, exclude
taskspec.goal: Extend the gateway from a PIT predicate to a whole-evidence admission decision: an EvidenceSnapshot is admissible for an as-of read only if its PIT is admissible AND its canonical identity reproduces AND its provenance does not contradict the snapshot. Where a caller presents an EvidenceRef, the ref must actually point at the snapshot it claims.
requirements: a snapshot whose recomputed snapshot_id does not reproduce is refused
a snapshot whose payload_hash does not reproduce is refused
an EvidenceRef that does not match its snapshot (id or content) is refused
provenance that names a different source than the snapshot is refused
PIT admissibility from task 1 is reused, not reimplemented
refusal reasons remain a closed machine-readable set

new_lesson_candidates: A result object that defines __bool__ around a domain meaning (admitted/valid/passed) makes truthiness checks ambiguous; prefer `is not None` for existence checks on such types.
observations: DETERMINISTIC VERIFICATION CAUGHT A REAL MODULE DEFECT, not just a test defect: pit_reason used truthiness on a decision object whose __bool__ returns `admitted`, so it returned None for every refusal. The GPT reviewer would very plausibly not have caught this from reading the diff; the failing assertion did. Evidence that the deterministic layer earns its place ahead of semantic review.
Hazard worth generalising: defining __bool__ on a result object makes `if obj` mean something other than 'exists', and any `if obj` on such a type is then suspect. Candidate lesson.
The 0B contract was STRICTER than assumed (source_adapter provenance requires source_id). Reading the contract's own validation rather than assuming its shape would have avoided two fixture failures.

An honest finding was preserved rather than smoothed: the gateway's provenance check is defence in depth because the 0B contract already enforces it at construction. Tests now assert both facts instead of implying the gateway is the primary guarantee.
